title: Federal-question jurisdiction
question: When does a case arise under federal law?

steps.note: A claim governed by local custom does not arise under the federal statute that lets it be brought.
Well-pleaded complaint: the federal issue must be part of the plaintiff’s own claim, not a defense.
Holmes’s creation test: a suit arises under the law that creates the cause of action.
A state-law claim can still qualify when it turns on a substantial federal question.
Four factors: necessarily raised, actually disputed, substantial, and no upset to the federal–state balance.
A legal-malpractice claim about a patent fails the substantiality and balance factors.
